A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SI-Attack and retain the same principal benchmarks and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original jailbreak experiments across eight MLLMs and three benchmarks, together with ablations, hidden-state analyses, and appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and reports additional mutation comparisons, adaptive-defense experiments, and sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Appendix D introduces an adaptive variant that screens candidates with a perplexity detector and uses trigram shuffling. The main shuffle-and-query method remains. Algorithm 1 also makes best-score bookkeeping explicit, consistent with the selection principle already stated in v1.

E1.justification: MM-safetybench, HADES, SafeBench, and their represented harmful tasks remain unchanged. V2 extends test scenarios to alternative input mutations and GPT-4o protected by a perplexity detector, without adding a dataset or application domain.

E2.justification: QR-Attack, HADES, and Figstep remain the principal attack comparators. Section 3.4 newly compares shuffling against text insertion, replacement, deletion, synonym and punctuation operations, and image masking, blurring, flipping, grayscale and solarization controls.

E3.justification: V2 adds mutation-control and Llama-3.1 perplexity-detector evaluation protocols. The PCA analysis changes from final-layer states of LLaVA-NEXT and InternVL-2 to multiple layers of InternVL-2. Additional settings include three queries, 9 and 25 image patches, and BPE-token shuffling. The principal benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: Section 3.4 tests whether inconsistency extends beyond shuffling, Appendix D tests adaptation to perplexity defense, and Tables 8, A.1 and B.1 extend sensitivity analyses. The original two-model PCA analysis is replaced by a layer-wise InternVL-2 analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report taking the highest toxic score from three random shuffles in Section 3.1. Neither introduces confidence intervals, variability estimates, significance tests, or additional repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: New results cover alternative mutations, layer-wise hidden states, adaptive defense, and additional ablation settings. Table D.1 reports a toxic score of 3.83 and ASR of 71.13% for adaptive SI-Attack against GPT-4o with a perplexity detector. Main Tables 1–7 and the relocated appendix benchmark tables retain their numerical results; the additions do not establish same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The new generic loss-minimization equation in Section 4 reformulates the existing judge-guided selection objective. It adds no substantive mathematical derivation, formal assumption, theorem, or proof. The word-shuffling, patch-shuffling, and ASR definitions retain their meaning.

C1.justification: The abstract, conclusion, and central shuffle-inconsistency contribution remain substantively unchanged. The introduction newly emphasizes effectiveness with few queries and claims that shuffling produces stronger inconsistency than the other tested mutations.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the earlier open-/closed-source mechanism discussion with a layer-depth interpretation, and adds speculation about semantic disruption explaining differences between mutations. It also explicitly interprets toxic scores as evidence of both comprehension and safety failure. The earlier caveat about limited access to closed-source internal mechanisms is omitted from this analysis.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link, Claude-3.5-Sonnet and Gemini-1.5-Pro version identifiers, and explicit identification of GPT-4o for the ablations. It specifies BPE tokenization and Llama-3.1 for the new tests. These disclosures do not establish changes to the previously reported experiments.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations concerning perplexity defenses, Llama 3, adversarial optimization, and safety-training failures, while removing SneakyPrompt. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain largely unchanged; consolidation of duplicate VLGuard references is bibliographic.

P1.justification: V2 revises portions of the introduction and Sections 3–5, renames Section 3.3, adds Section 3.4 and Appendix D, and expands the method explanation. Most existing prose and the overall organization remain recognizable. The author list also changes.

P2.justification: Figure 3 changes from two model-level plots to eight layer-level panels. V2 adds the mutation-comparison Figure 4 and defense Table D.1, expands several ablation tables, and revises captions. Existing benchmark tables, the framework illustration, case studies, and judge prompt are retained with renumbering and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful mutation controls, adaptive-defense evidence, sensitivity checks, and reproducibility information while retaining the original benchmark results. These improve support and documentation. The revised PCA trades two-model breadth for layer-level depth, and the new defense experiment covers only one benchmark subset, so the overall gain is limited.
